message: Morning both, and welcome to day one of PulseAnalytics. Kickoff at 9.30, then the epic-cutting workshop straight after. Two things I want us to agree before we write any code: what we are building first, and what we are deliberately not building yet.
Ready. I have a blank repo and strong opinions about .gitignore.
Same, minus the gitignore opinions. I have been through the BRD twice - the recurring theme is that nobody trusts the current numbers rather than that they are missing numbers.

Workshop done. Eleven epics, PULSE-1 through PULSE-11. The sequencing argument we settled on: ingest, then define, then trust, then model, then show. Dashboards are epic five of eleven and that is deliberate.

The bit I want to flag for future-us: PULSE-10 runs the whole length of the project rather than being a deployment phase at the end. A deployment story started in month seven is a deployment story that discovers the code cannot be deployed.
And no dashboard until epic five. I want that written somewhere more durable than a Slack message, because in about four weeks somebody is going to ask why there is nothing to look at.

It is in the PULSE-2 epic description as an explicit non-goal. And you are right that someone will ask - the answer is that a dashboard built on a metric nobody has agreed to just locks in the disagreement.

[PULSE-19] Metric workshop report, and it went worse than I hoped, which is the good outcome. Finance excludes shipping from revenue. Marketing includes it. The board deck has been built from the marketing figure for two quarters. That is about a 6% difference on the monthly number.
[PULSE-19] Nobody had noticed because the two figures have never appeared on the same page as each other.
Asking the uncomfortable question early: are we the team that tells the board the last two decks were 6% high?

Yes, but framed as 'here is the standard definition and here is the restated series', not as an accusation. Restating is a one-off cost. Two live definitions is a permanent one, and it gets more expensive every month we leave it.

[PULSE-25] Writing the AOV definition into the KPI doc now, before the facts exist. AOV is revenue over distinct completed orders, header grain, never averaged from lines. Flagging it early because there is no error message for averaging the wrong grain - you just get a plausible wrong number.
[PULSE-25] Noted. I suspect we will still hit it once anyway.

Weekly numbers CSV attached, week ending 20 Mar. Still no dashboard, deliberately - we are agreeing definitions first, and the CSV plus a conversation is doing that job better than a chart would. Revenue here is on the agreed definition: net of discounts, excluding shipping and tax.

[PULSE-24] To the question from finance in the thread - yes, this figure will differ from the marketing dashboard by roughly 6%, and that difference is the shipping treatment. It is written up in docs/kpi-definitions.md and I am happy to walk anyone through it.

[PULSE-4] Star schema is done. 'Revenue by region by month for electronics' went from a day of bespoke SQL to about four minutes. Next sprint we finally build a dashboard - fourteen weeks in, which was the plan.
